subject: geography
title: KS3 Geography — Settlements
subtitle: Revision pack for settlement sites, functions, patterns, hierarchy and sustainability
description: A source-faithful KS3 geography pack covering why settlements develop, how they are classified, and how places can become more sustainable. It includes key terminology, applied recall, ordering tasks and reading comprehension based on the supplied study pack.

data.sourceTitle: Why Early Settlements Developed In Certain Places
data.targetTitle: Why Early Settlements Developed In Certain Places
data.sourcePassage: Early settlements were rarely built by accident. People looked for reliable water, flat land and fertile soil so that they could drink, farm and build more easily. They also valued shelter from harsh weather and sites that were easier to defend, such as hilltops or bends in rivers. Nearby wood, stone or clay reduced the effort needed to build homes. A good situation mattered as well. Settlements linked to rivers, roads or harbours could trade more easily and often grew faster than isolated places.

questions.question: Name two physical factors that made a site attractive for an early settlement.
questions.modelAnswer: Possible answers include water supply, flat land, fertile soil, shelter, defence or nearby building materials.

questions.question: Which detail from the passage is about situation rather than site?
Why could a settlement with better transport links grow faster?
questions.modelAnswer: Better transport links make it easier to trade, move people and bring in resources, so the settlement becomes more connected and attractive.

questions.question: Explain why geographers need to consider both site and situation when studying settlements.
questions.modelAnswer: Site explains the physical land chosen for building, while situation explains how the place connects to surrounding routes and settlements. Both help explain growth and importance.

data.sourcePassage: Settlements do not all look the same or serve the same purpose. A linear settlement develops in a line, often along a road, river or valley. A nucleated settlement has clustered buildings, which can help people share resources and feel protected. A dispersed settlement has buildings spread out across a rural area, often where farming land is widely spaced. Functions also vary. Some settlements act as ports, market towns or tourist resorts, while others are mainly residential. Large cities can have several functions at once, such as administration, tourism, finance and housing.

questions.question: What is the main visual feature of a nucleated settlement?
questions.modelAnswer: Its buildings are clustered closely together.

questions.question: Which settlement pattern is most likely along a river valley?
Why might a city have more than one function?
questions.modelAnswer: Cities are large and well connected, so they can support many activities such as government, shopping, tourism, housing and transport.

questions.question: Explain one reason why a dispersed pattern might suit a rural area.
questions.modelAnswer: Rural areas often have more land and lower population density, so homes and farms can be spread out instead of clustered together.

data.sourcePassage: The settlement hierarchy ranks places from isolated dwellings and hamlets up to villages, towns, cities and conurbations. The higher a settlement is in the hierarchy, the more people and services it usually has. Small settlements often provide low-order services such as a corner shop or a primary school because people need them frequently and want them nearby. Cities can support high-order services such as universities, specialist hospitals and airports because they have a larger threshold population and a wider sphere of influence. As urbanisation increases, more people move into towns and cities for jobs, education and services.

questions.question: Which type of service is most likely to be found in a village: high-order or low-order?
questions.modelAnswer: Low-order services are more likely to be found in a village.

questions.question: Why can cities support airports and universities?
options: They have a larger threshold population
questions.modelAnswer: They have a larger threshold population

questions.question: How does sphere of influence help explain why a city is more important than a small village?
questions.modelAnswer: A city serves people from a much larger area, so more people travel to it for specialist services and jobs than would travel to a village.

questions.question: Explain one possible consequence of urbanisation for a growing city.
questions.modelAnswer: Urbanisation can increase traffic, pollution, waste or housing shortages because more people and activity are concentrated in the city.

data.sourcePassage: A sustainable settlement meets people’s needs without damaging the environment or reducing opportunities for future generations. This means planners must think about environmental, social and economic factors together. Public transport, safe cycle routes and walking paths can reduce car use. Green spaces improve recreation, air quality and wildlife habitats. Renewable energy and energy-efficient housing help lower emissions. Planned developments such as Milton Keynes show how roads, green space and services can be organised carefully, while BedZED is used as an eco-development example with solar energy, water recycling and efficient homes. Sustainable development still brings challenges because it can be expensive and difficult to manage.

questions.question: Which three types of factors should planners balance in a sustainable settlement?
Which example from the passage is an eco-development in London?
Why is public transport important in a sustainable settlement?
questions.modelAnswer: It reduces dependence on cars, which can cut traffic congestion and air pollution while making travel more efficient.

questions.question: Explain why sustainability is not only about protecting the environment.
questions.modelAnswer: A settlement also needs to be socially fair and economically successful, so people can access services, housing and jobs as well as a cleaner environment.
